title: Inference Runbook and Incident Drill Obligations Annex
content:
Purpose:
This annex specifies operational runbook obligations and recurring incident-drill commitments for vendors that provide managed inference services to Redwood Inference customers. The goal is to ensure vendors can demonstrate repeatable, auditable incident handling and recovery practices for inference-specific failure modes (e.g., KV cache corruption, model-rollback, degraded tail latency, and telemetry loss).

Scope and applicability:
Applies to any third-party or partner ("Vendor") that: (a) hosts inference endpoints for Redwood customers; (b) provides critical tooling (KV caches, prefix caches, or routing services) integrated with Redwood-managed control planes; or (c) acts as a subsupplier in a Dedicated or Private deployment contract.

Definitions (selected):
- Control Plane Incident: an event that materially prevents placement, routing, or metadata operations required to serve inference requests.
- Inference Degradation: sustained tail-latency increase beyond SLOs, token-generation stall, or KV cache staleness resulting in customer-visible errors.
- Drill: an orchestrated, documented simulation of an incident, executed with telemetry capture and post-mortem artifacts.

Vendor obligations (runbook maintenance):
1) Runbook baseline: Vendor must maintain a written inference-runbook covering: detection triggers, triage checklists, containment steps (including safe model-rollback), KV cache invalidation patterns, telemetry retention points for forensics, and post-incident evidence preservation steps. The runbook must be readable by a qualified SRE with no prior vendor context.
2) Versioning and access: Runbook must be versioned with changelog and made available to Redwood via the secure evidence portal. Each substantive change must be notified to Redwood within five business days and linked to a Jira ticket.

Drill schedule and minimums:
1) Annual tabletop: At least one company-wide tabletop drill per 12 months that walks through a Control Plane Incident scenario and documents decision points, communications, and time-to-decision metrics.
2) Quarterly technical drills: Four per year focused on inference-layer failure modes (KV cache corruption, model weight mismatch, sudden GPU OOM under batching). At least one drill per year must be executed against a production-like environment with synthetic traffic.
3) Post-change drills: Following any major change to model-serving infrastructure (e.g., new kernel, quantization rollout, or routing policy change), the Vendor must run a targeted drill within 30 days to validate rollback and fallback paths.
4) Surprise capability verification: Redwood reserves the right to request an unannounced verification drill with 72 hours notice up to once per policy year; Vendor must accommodate within operational safety limits.

Drill execution requirements:
- Pre-drill plan: Written objectives, success criteria, and telemetry capture plan submitted to Redwood at least 7 business days prior to planned drill.
- Role participation: SREs and on-call owners for serving runtime, platform orchestration, and security must participate; vendor must provide name and contact for each role.
- Evidence capture: Complete set of logs, traces, span-level traces for a 2-hour window around the drill, config snapshots, and a timestamped runbook entry. Evidence must be preserved for 180 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Safety and customer impact: Drills must avoid customer data leakage and minimize impact; production-like drills must be executed against synthetic tenants or agreed maintenance windows.

Post-drill deliverables and remediation:
1) Post-Drill Report: Vendor must deliver a report within 5 business days containing: timeline of actions, gap analysis, list of runbook edits, and a remediation plan with owners and target dates.
2) Remediation SLA: Critical gaps (security, data-loss, inability to execute safe rollback) must have remediation completion within 30 calendar days. High-impact but non-critical items within 90 days.
3) Evidence of remediation: For each remediation item, Vendor must provide validation artifacts (replay logs, updated test harness results, PR links) and mark runbook entries as verified.

Validation and audit rights:
- Redwood may perform annual audits of the vendor's runbook, drill artifacts, and remediation evidence. Audits may include remote evidence review and up to two days of on-site review per year, subject to agreed-notice and safety rules.
- Vendor must provide sandbox access or replay harness data on a curated subset of synthetic requests to allow Redwood to validate detection and rollback logic.

Escalation and communications:
- Notification: Vendor must alert Redwood’s SIRT within 60 minutes of detection of any Control Plane Incident or Inference Degradation that meets the vendor’s incident-severity criteria.
- War-room: For incidents declared Sev-2 or higher, Vendor must establish a war-room within 2 hours and invite Redwood technical leads. War-room notes become part of incident evidence.
- Customer notifications: If customer data scope or availability is impacted, Vendor must provide a communications timeline aligned to Redwood’s customer-notification protocols.

Failure to comply and remedies:
- Remediation hold: Repeated failure (two or more missed drill obligations in a 12-month period or failure to remediate a critical gap within 30 days) permits Redwood to require: (a) third-party verification at Vendor expense; (b) temporary suspension of onboarding new customer routes; or (c) contract termination for material breach after cure period.
- Credits: If a drill deficiency is tied to an incident that results in customer downtime, Redwood may seek service credits under the master services schedule.

Confidentiality and evidence handling:
- All drill artifacts and runbook snapshots exchanged under this annex are Confidential Information and may only be used for contractual validation, audits, and authorized remediation. Redwood may share selected redacted artifacts with customers where required for compliance but will coordinate with Vendor.

Insurance and liability considerations:
- Vendor must maintain cyber-insurance and professional liability coverages consistent with the master agreement; proof of coverage and an updated COI must be provided annually and within 10 business days of request.
- Nothing in this annex limits contractually agreed indemnities for negligent runbook maintenance or willful misrepresentation of drill results.

Appendix A — Minimum drill playbook checklist (to be included in runbook):
- Objective and scope statement
- Detection trigger list and alert thresholds
- Initial containment steps with exact CLI/API commands (sanitized)
- Safe model-rollback procedure and verification steps
- KV cache snapshot & restore procedure and data retention notes
- Telemetry capture points and tracing levels
- External communications template (internal, Redwood SIRT, affected customers)
- Post-mortem template with RCA fields and corrective action owners

Notes and negotiation points for commercial teams:
- Redwood prefers at least quarterly drills with one production-like validation per year; Vendor proposals to reduce cadence must justify compensating controls (automated rollback tests, higher QA coverage, or independent attestations).
- For small vendors or specialized subsuppliers, Redwood will accept a scaled drill cadence if supplemented by continuous CI-driven rollback tests and documentary evidence of automated canary checks.

Sign-off:
This annex is intended to be attached to the Master Service Agreement between Redwood Inference and the Vendor. Signatures by authorized representatives from both parties will render this annex effective as of the last date signed in the main agreement.

-- End of annex --
